metadata.name: trading
metadata.description: Continuum trading accounts: Hyperliquid-style trade-only session keys over Manifest order books

instructions.name: claim_seat
docs: Claim the trader's seat on a market, which Manifest needs before
deposits and resting orders. The trader PDA pays the rent.

accounts.name: mr_market
docs: The Continuum market whose token this book trades.

instructions.name: commit_order
docs: Commit an order from the trading account. It fills at the next official
price, or after its time to live anyone can refund it; either way the
tokens and the rent come back to the trader PDA, never anywhere else.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Move tokens from the owner's wallet into the trading account.

accounts.name: owner_token
docs: The owner's own associated token account for this mint.

accounts.name: trader_token
docs: The trader PDA's associated token account for this mint.

instructions.name: deposit_to_market
docs: Move tokens from the trader's token account into its seat on a market.

accounts.name: trader_token
docs: The trader PDA's associated token account for this mint.

instructions.name: open_account
docs: Create the owner's trading account. The trader PDA needs no account of
its own; the owner funds it with SOL for Manifest seat rent.

instructions.name: place_orders
docs: Cancel and place resting orders from the seat's balance. Session-signed
orders must be priced inside the band and under the per-order limit.

instructions.name: revoke_session
docs: Revoke the session key at once. Owner only.

instructions.name: set_session
docs: Grant (or replace) the session key. Owner only.

instructions.name: swap_pool
docs: Swap on the CLP's bin book from the trading account. The book trades
only while the market floats; the CLP enforces that. A session-signed
swap must fill inside the band, judged on what actually moved, so a
stolen key cannot force a fill deep into the book.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Move tokens from the trading account back to the owner's wallet. The
owner or the session key may sign: the only destination is the owner's
own associated token account, so a stolen key cannot take anything.

accounts.name: owner_token
docs: The owner's own associated token account for this mint.

accounts.name: trader_token
docs: The trader PDA's associated token account for this mint.

instructions.name: withdraw_from_market
docs: Move tokens from the trader's seat on a market back to its token account.

accounts.name: trader_token
docs: The trader PDA's associated token account for this mint.

instructions.name: withdraw_sol
docs: Return SOL the trader PDA holds for rent to the owner. Owner only. The
PDA must keep its rent-exempt minimum unless emptied completely.

fields.name: initial_s_price

fields.name: mint_fee_bps
docs: Mint fee in basis points (e.g., 10 = 0.1%)

fields.name: redeem_fee_bps
docs: Redeem fee in basis points

fields.name: total_l_supply
docs: Total supply of Long tokens. Paired mint/redeem keeps this equal to
`total_s_supply`; single-side keeper mint/redeem (`keeper_mint_single`,
see lib.rs) intentionally moves only one side, so the two supplies can
diverge — a first-order (directional) delta the γ decay does NOT charge.

fields.name: total_s_supply
docs: Total supply of Short tokens. Equal to `total_l_supply` under paired
mint/redeem, but single-side keeper mint/redeem deliberately lets it
diverge (see `total_l_supply` above).

fields.name: total_collateral
docs: Total collateral locked (sum across all vaults)

fields.name: risk_state
docs: Current risk state (updated by keepers from oracle)

fields.name: risk_state_updated_at
docs: Last time risk state was updated

fields.name: risk_fee_config
docs: Risk-based fee configuration

fields.name: user_twap_price
docs: TWAP price for user quoting (updated by keepers)

fields.name: twap_updated_at
docs: Last TWAP update time

fields.name: worst_case_config
docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting

fields.name: oracle_confidence
docs: Oracle confidence interval (updated by keepers)

fields.name: keeper_authority
docs: Whitelisted keeper authority that is allowed to update risk state

fields.name: dev_tax_pct
docs: Dev tax percentage (updated by keeper based on CLP TVL tiers)

fields.name: yield_ceiling_bps
docs: Maximum fraction of total_collateral deployable to yield protocols (basis points).
Default: 6000 (60%). Remaining 40% stays liquid to cover redemptions.

fields.name: deployed_to_yield
docs: Amount of collateral currently deployed to external lending protocols.
Invariant: deployed_to_yield <= total_collateral * yield_ceiling_bps / 10_000

fields.name: total_yield_harvested
docs: Cumulative yield harvested to CLP vault (never decrements, informational).

fields.name: yield_enabled
docs: Whether collateral yield deployment is enabled for this market.

fields.name: buffer_target_bps
docs: Keeper-posted overcollateralization buffer (bps OVER parity) — the dynamic
solvency target. Target ratio = 10_000 + buffer_target_bps, clamped to
[MIN_BUFFER_BPS, MAX_BUFFER_BPS]. 0 (legacy/unset) is treated as the default
200 (102%) by `target_ratio_bps()`, so old accounts behave as before until the
keeper posts a value. Sized from σ-regime + live inventory (vol_model::dynamic_buffer).

fields.name: s_gamma_index
docs: Keeper-posted decay scalar on the SHORT NAV, in 1e9 fixed point
(1_000_000_000 = 1.0 = no decay). The effective short NAV is
`(K / l_nav) · s_gamma_index / 1e9`. It only ever ratchets DOWN, by the
realized variance the short pair accrues, so holding the short across a
choppy path costs the decay — which banks as collateral surplus (the
long leg is never touched). `0` (legacy/unset) is read as 1e9 by
`short_gamma_index()`, so old accounts behave exactly as before until
the keeper posts a value. NOT a perp funding rate — there is no periodic
cash transfer; it is a structural mark on the short token's value, so the
1:1 paired round-trip and buy-and-hold mechanics are unchanged at a fixed γ.

fields.name: gamma_day_start_ts
docs: Unix ts the current γ day-bucket opened. 0 = no bucket yet.

fields.name: gamma_day_decay_1e9
docs: γ index units (1e9) decayed inside the current day-bucket. TELEMETRY
ONLY — tracked so an auditor can see the day's total, never enforced.

fields.name: gamma_last_write_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last accepted γ write. Lets an auditor alarm on writer
SILENCE — the failure mode no cap can catch, because it looks like calm.

fields.name: gamma_epoch
docs: Bumped by a re-anchor. Carried in `SetGammaParams` as a CAS so a decay
post computed against a pre-re-anchor γ can never land after the fold
and re-charge the whole epoch.

fields.name: reanchor_count
docs: How many re-anchors this market has seen. 0 = never.

fields.name: genesis_s_price
docs: `initial_s_price` as of genesis, before any re-anchor folded γ into it.
Backfilled lazily on the first re-anchor; 0 = never re-anchored, so the
live `initial_s_price` IS the genesis value.

fields.name: last_reanchor_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last re-anchor. 0 = never.

fields.name: short_payoff_cap_c_1e9
docs: Reserved for the capped short payoff `S = γ·min(K/P, C·K/P₀)` (1e9
fixed). The instruction ships in upgrade #2; the FIELD lands here so
that upgrade is instructions-only and needs no second realloc.
0 = unset = uncapped, i.e. exactly today's behavior.

fields.name: price_adjust_den
docs: Denominator of the cumulative corporate-action ratio. See
`price_adjust_num`. 0 = unset = identity.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_num
docs: A corporate action ARMED AHEAD of its ex-date: the cumulative pair that
becomes live at `price_adjust_effective_ts`. Until then the current
`price_adjust_num/den` keeps applying.
This exists because arming a ratio early is otherwise actively harmful,
not merely useless. The adjustment multiplies the NEXT raw print, and
before the ex-date that print is still PRE-split — so an early 2:1 would
double the stored price, the 25% move guard would reject every push, and
the market would halt from the moment of arming until the split actually
happened. Gating on a timestamp is what makes "schedule it weeks ahead"
a true statement instead of a longer outage.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_den
docs: Denominator of the pending pair. See `price_adjust_pending_num`.

fields.name: price_adjust_effective_ts
docs: Unix ts from which the pending pair applies. 0 = nothing pending.
Set it to the ex-date OPEN — the first instant a venue quotes the
post-action price. Misalignment is bounded and self-correcting for
ratios above ~1.333: a print on the wrong side of the boundary is
REJECTED by the 25% guard, not absorbed, so an early or late `ts` costs
rejected pushes rather than a mispriced book. Below ~1.333 nothing
rejects it and the alignment is the only control.

fields.name: price_adjust_last_effective_ts
docs: Most recent activated units boundary, retained after promotion and rescheduling.

fields.name: fill_or_kill
docs: With one immediate-or-cancel order and no cancels: revert unless it
fills in full. A market order that must not fill in part.

types.name: PlaceOrder
docs: Borsh-identical to Manifest's `PlaceOrderParams` (order_type is its enum's
one-byte discriminant).

types.name: Pool
docs: v2 native DISCRETE-BIN quote book for ONE synth side (long or short) vs
cUSDC. `asks`/`bids` are per-bin reserves around `base_price_1e6` (≈ side
NAV), priced at `base·r^±k` with `r = 1 + step_bps/1e4`. Swaps walk the bins
(real slippage); the keeper repositions to NAV with a skewed shape via
`set_pool_shape`. See `clmm.rs`.
NAMING: despite the `CLMM_*` env vars and the `clmm.rs` filename, this is
NOT a Uniswap-v3-style concentrated-liquidity AMM. There is no continuous
`x·y=k` curve and no permissionless LPs: each bin holds a fixed reserve at a
fixed price (constant-sum within a bin), and the ladder is POSTED by the
keeper rather than emerging from deposits. It is a discrete-bin liquidity
book (Trader Joe "Liquidity Book" / Meteora DLMM family — `clmm.rs` calls
its own math "DLMM-style"), with a single quoter. The old names are kept for
config compatibility; docs say "bin book".

types.name: PoolSwapArgs
docs: A swap on the CLP's bin book for one side of a market.

docs: 0 buys the token with cUSDC, 1 sells it for cUSDC.

types.name: RiskFeeConfig
docs: Configuration for risk-based fee adjustments

fields.name: proxy_fee_multiplier
docs: Fee multiplier for Proxy Mode (100 = 1x, 200 = 2x)

fields.name: stress_fee_multiplier
docs: Fee multiplier for Stress mode (100 = 1x, 300 = 3x)
Also the starting point for Recovery Dutch auction (decays to 1.0x over 1 hour)

fields.name: stress_mint_cap
docs: Mint cap per transaction in Stress mode (0 = disabled)

fields.name: allow_mint_in_stress
docs: Whether to allow new mints in Stress mode

fields.name: allow_redeem_in_stress
docs: Whether to allow redeems in Stress mode

types.name: RiskState
docs: Risk state for graduated oracle gating (mirrors oracle program)

types.name: TradingRules
docs: One per owner wallet. Holds the trading rules; the funds sit with `trader`,
a data-less PDA that is the Manifest trader (it owns the token accounts and
the seats, and pays seat rent from SOL the owner sends it).

fields.name: owner
docs: The main wallet: the only signer that can withdraw (and only to itself)
or change the session.

fields.name: session_key
docs: A key that can trade but never withdraw. `Pubkey::default()` when none.

fields.name: max_order_quote
docs: The most quote (cUSDC atoms) one session-signed order may commit.

types.name: WorstCaseQuotingConfig
docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting
Protects protocol from informed traders exploiting confidence interval edges

fields.name: enabled
docs: Whether worst-case quoting is enabled

fields.name: normal_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Normal state (100 = 1x, 150 = 1.5x)

fields.name: proxy_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Proxy state

fields.name: stress_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Stress state (also the starting point for Recovery Dutch auction)
